heads.reason: Most terms describe a deity or sacred things, though holy, spiritual and theistic can describe a religious person.

heads.title: Angel
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Angelic and saintly describe a person's goodness of character, though cherubic describes looks.

heads.title: Satan
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Devilish, satanic and diabolic readily describe a person's cruel or wicked character.

heads.title: Jupiter
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Its adjectives (god-like, fairy-like, sylph-like) mainly describe appearance or grace rather than a person's character.

heads.title: Demon
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Mixed: impish, fiendish, elfish and demonic can describe a person's nature, while spectral, ghostly, haunted and uncanny describe things or atmosphere.

heads.title: Heaven
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Heavenly, celestial, supernal and elysian describe things, places or states, with only beatific occasionally suiting a person's manner.

heads.title: Hell
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Hellish, infernal and stygian describe conditions, places or deeds rather than what a person is like.

heads.title: Theology
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Religious describes a person's faith, but theological and denominational mostly describe systems or bodies of doctrine.

heads.title: Orthodoxy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Orthodox, faithful, sound, Christian, evangelical and monotheistic all readily describe a person's belief or affiliation.

heads.title: Heterodoxy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Heretical, heathen, pagan, dissident, recusant, dissenting, sectarian and gentile describe people by belief or group membership.

heads.title: Judeo-Christian Revelation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Scriptural, biblical, apostolic and canonical mostly describe texts, revelation or doctrine rather than a person.

heads.title: Pseudo-Revelation
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Piety
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Pious, devout, godly, humble, saintly, reverent and faithful are ordinary descriptions of a person's character and devotion.

heads.title: Impiety
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Impious, profane, sanctimonious, unctuous, pharisaical, bigoted and fanatical describe a person's attitudes and conduct.

heads.title: Irreligion
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Irreligious, godless, atheistic, skeptical, freethinking, faithless and worldly describe a person's beliefs and outlook.

heads.title: Worship
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Devout and reverent describe a person, but devotional, solemn and pure mostly describe acts or things.

heads.title: Idolatry
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Its single adjective, idolatrous, can describe a person's practice or attitude, though only narrowly.

heads.title: Sorcery
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Magic, mystic, cabalistic, voodoo and talismanic describe practices or objects, with only Circean and mystic occasionally describing a person.

heads.title: Spell
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Sorcerer
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Churchdom
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Episcopalian, papal, Roman, Popish, monkish and priestly describe people by church membership or office, while most others describe the institution.

heads.title: Clergy
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Ordained, in orders and the Reverend describe a person's clerical status or title, while the rest are formal designations.

heads.title: Laity
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Lay and secular describe a person's standing as a non-cleric, while civil, temporal and laical mostly describe matters rather than people.

heads.title: Rite
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Ritual, ceremonial and baptismal describe rites and acts rather than the person performing them.

heads.title: Canonicals
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers

heads.title: Temple
heads.class_title: Words relating to the sentient and moral powers
heads.reason: Cloistered and monastic can describe a sheltered or monastic way of life, but claustral, monasterial and conventual describe buildings or institutions.
